elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 14.1 contains no affiliate carve-out; the only no-consent exception is for "the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement." An affiliate transfer therefore still needs Vendor's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: "either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent". Note two retained narrowings: the asset test is limited to assets "related to this Agreement", and consent is still required where the transaction involves a direct competitor of Vendor; the added "upon prior written notice" is a notice, not a consent, condition.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The consent requirement is mutual, but the retained "Notwithstanding the foregoing" sentence lets Vendor assign in its own merger/acquisition/asset sale "without such consent", so Vendor can assign without Customer's consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted in the first sentence: "without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld."

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Retained proviso only conditions such a transfer on consent — "except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required" — rather than prohibiting it; and Customer's consent to that assignment is now expressly subject to a reasonableness standard.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: No change-of-control termination or re-pricing right appears in § 14.1 or in the termination triggers identified (breach and insolvency only); nothing in the redline creates one, so the condition does not arise.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: "either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent" — expressly mutual and retained unchanged.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Operation 2 inserts "upon prior written notice to the other party" into the successor carve-out, so the no-consent successor transfer runs on prior written notice both ways.

"Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party." No no-consent non-successor exception (no affiliate exception) is retained or added, so all non-successor assignments still need consent; "Any assignment in violation of this Section 14.1 shall be null and void" backstops it.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 adds "which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld" to the general consent sentence, which governs all non-successor assignments.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: mutual successor right (retained), prior written notice (added), consent for all other assignments (retained), and a reasonableness standard on that consent (added).

Preferred level is not reached: no affiliate no-consent carve-out for Customer, Vendor retains a no-consent successor assignment right, and the competitor restriction is consent-based rather than an absolute bar on assignment to a Customer competitor. Correctly not pursued, since a Customer affiliate exception would collide with the fallback element requiring consent for all non-successor assignments.

Deviation status is right: before the edit the clause failed the fallback on two material terms (no reasonableness standard on consent, no notice mechanic for the successor carve-out); it is not walk-away because there is a mutual M&A carve-out and no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on Customer's change of control.

Minimal: two short in-line insertions, no deletions, no survival tails, expense language, or procedures; the favourable retained language (mutual competitor-consent proviso, null-and-void sentence, successors-and-assigns sentence) is untouched.

Preserves intent: mutuality, the competitor proviso, and the invalidity remedy all survive without contradiction; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created. Minor residual worth noting in the rationale only (not a deviation): the added reasonableness standard sits in the first sentence and arguably does not reach the separate competitor-consent proviso, and the asset test remains "assets related to this Agreement" rather than all assets.
